title: The ULTIMATE Triceps Exercises Tier-List (Mythical-tier to Toothpick-tier)
summary: NH ranks 30+ triceps exercises from Mythical (S) to Toothpick (D) tier, based on long-head stretch, elbow tendinitis risk, comfort, grip and progressability. Cable extensions and pushdowns dominate the top, compound presses rank low for triceps, and kickbacks, bench dips, Tate press and bench press land in toothpick tier.
claims: Tier criteria: mythical-tier triceps exercises work all three heads properly, are low fatigue for the elbow, can be spammed, are fun and easy to set up
Toothpick-tier exercises are dangerous for the elbow, tendinitis-prone, or barely work the triceps
The dumbbell French press is excellent but run heavy for too long it inevitably causes elbow tendinitis; done with the back against an incline bench it becomes mythical
The overhead cable extension can be progressed for two years to build a huge long head without problems: no rebound, no head collision, freer shoulder path
Close-grip bench alone gives disappointing triceps for most people; it is the best horizontal press for triceps but compounds prioritize the strongest muscles (chest, shoulders)
Exercises that rank high for triceps tend to train the long head, which is where most of the mass is, and most presses do not work it enough
Reverse-grip pushdowns are underrated; letting the arm rise as you extend brings in plenty of long head, but the wrist can become the limiting factor
EZ-bar skull crushers to the forehead are overrated and probably the worst tricep movement for elbow tendinitis (golfer's elbow) due to tension on the tendon at the bottom
The standing EZ-bar overhead extension is mostly ego lifting: you can almost double the weight because shoulders turn it into a press
Ego lifting is using more weight than an exercise can turn into a justified stimulus
Cable skull crushers fix most EZ-bar issues: deeper flexion, tension stays behind you rather than on stacked joints; but beware heavy loads, he knew two naturals who tore a triceps on it
The JM press combines the best of skull crusher and close-grip bench, building long head with carryover to pressing; start with very light weight to learn the form
V-bar pushdowns remain a standard because they let you load heavy safely; best for the lateral head, they still recruit some long head
He is not science-based; he bases advice on his own experience, e.g. rope pushdowns feel tremendous despite strength-curve critiques
Rotate V-bar and rope pushdowns: near one-to-one carryover while the slight differences in elbow angle prevent tendinitis
Swiss/football bar bench lets the elbows travel further back for more triceps; close-grip on it could be excellent tier
Properly done dips with forward lean are mostly chest and shoulders; only doing dips for triceps will disappoint
If grip can become a limiting factor, a triceps movement loses points
Bodyweight triceps extensions build the long head but rely on balance, which is risky for a fragile, tendinitis-prone elbow; fine for skilled calisthenics athletes
Bench dips are a noob exercise: awkward wrists, internal rotation, no good stretch or squeeze; intermediates have all moved on
Dumbbell pullovers give only passive long-head stretch; always include some movement with elbow flexion/extension for the long head
Any setup that forces acrobatic positions (like the standing rope push-away fighting the stack) loses points; the kneeling cable extension gives the same angle comfortably
Finding your ideal kneeling cable extension setup takes several workouts of experimenting, but once found you can keep it for life
Dumbbell kickbacks are garbage and a noob trap: unbalanced, tension only at the top; if you like the motion, use cables which provide tension throughout
The Tate press combines everything wrong with presses and extensions: limited ROM, bad for wrist, stress on tendon; historically used for shoulders not triceps
Dumbbell skull crushers beat EZ-bar ones because the dumbbells can travel past the head for a deeper stretch
Cross-body cable extension is good (not the best): works all three heads, very elbow friendly; use a proper handle, not the bare carabiner
Floor triceps extension keeps elbows pointing up at the bottom: tendinitis risk and poor stretch
Triceps dips with a vertical torso, only doing the top portion, shift load to the triceps; do not go deep or you risk the shoulders
Cables suit how the triceps function and spare the tendon, but give less overall stimulus and get boring; mix excellent free-weight and mythical cable movements
Machine triceps extensions on chest machines, assisted dip machines and seated dip machines are mediocre; assisted dips are at best a finisher
Floor press trains lockout but lockout does not grow triceps as much as people think
Lying triceps extension with the shoulder in full flexion (bar behind the head) is his favorite and the only free-weight mythical-tier exercise
Band pushdowns are mediocre for hypertrophy (hard to overload) but are the cure for triceps tendinitis when done high rep, high volume, high frequency
A friend did 100 reps of single-arm pushdowns at the end of every session for five years, progressively overloading, and had the biggest triceps he has seen
The bench press is not a triceps builder; failing a lockout is due to poor chest velocity, not weak triceps
Pick triceps exercises that are tendon-friendly, comfortable and progressable long term, and that together develop all three heads
